clips.send: Painted pottery basin. Painted pottery from Banpo (enlarged). Banpo people made beautiful painted pottery: black patterns painted on red pottery. The famous basin shows human faces and fish, painted on the inside. Fish patterns suggest that fishing was also a source of food.

clips.send: Mortise-and-tenon joint. Timbers lock together without nails. Wooden parts with mortise-and-tenon joints were found at Hemudu. One part sticks out (the tenon) and fits into a hole (the mortise), locking the timbers firmly together. This became a key technique of traditional Chinese timber buildings and is still used today.

clips.send: Hemudu stilt house. Raised on wooden piles above wet ground. The Hemudu site is in Yuyao, Zhejiang, in the Yangtze River valley, about 7,000 years old. Wooden piles were driven into the ground, beams and floorboards laid on top, then the house built above: a stilt (ganlan-style) house. The south is warm, wet and rainy. A raised floor stays dry, lets air flow, and keeps out snakes and insects.

clips.send: Millet field. A drought-tolerant crop for the dry north. Banpo people grew millet (粟, foxtail millet). China is one of the first countries in the world to grow millet. They farmed with polished stone tools such as stone axes, spades and knives, grew vegetables and raised pigs and dogs.

clips.send: 河姆渡：干栏式房屋。 用木桩把房子架离潮湿的地面。 河姆渡遗址位于浙江余姚，地处长江流域，距今约 7000 年。 先在地上打下木桩，架上横梁、铺上地板，再在上面盖房子——这就是“干栏式房屋”。 南方温暖湿润、雨水多，房屋架空可以防潮、通风，还能防虫蛇野兽。

clips.send: 河姆渡：水稻。 喜水的南方作物。 河姆渡遗址出土了大量稻谷、稻壳，说明河姆渡人种植水稻。 我国是世界上最早种植水稻的国家之一。 水稻需要大量的水，适合温暖湿润的长江流域。
clips.text: 河姆渡：水稻。 喜水的南方作物。 河姆渡遗址出土了大量稻谷、稻壳，说明河姆渡人种植水稻。。 我国是世界上最早种植水稻的国家之一。。 水稻需要大量的水，适合温暖湿润的长江流域。

clips.send: 河姆渡：榫卯结构。 不用钉子就能把木头接牢。 河姆渡遗址发现了带有榫卯的木构件。 一凸（榫）一凹（卯）相互咬合，把木头牢牢连在一起。 榫卯成为我国传统木结构建筑的重要技术，一直沿用至今。

clips.send: 半坡：屋内灶坑。 用来取暖和烧煮食物。 房屋中间有灶坑，可以取暖、照明、烧煮食物。 固定的灶坑说明人们过着定居生活。 用火的历史更早：北京人就已经会使用天然火。
